newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean opposition calls for fresh Hanbo probe.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean opposition calls for fresh Hanbo probe.

text.p: South Korea's opposition on Thursday demanded a fresh probe into a loan scandal involving failed Hanbo Steel Co, lashing out at state prosecutors for what it called a "disappointing" investigation.
Shin Nak-yun, vice president of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics, told parliament that her party would ask independent prosecutors to restart the investigation.

Announcing the outcome of nearly a month of investigation, state prosecutors on Wednesday indicted 10 people, including a former cabinet minister and three ruling party lawmakers, in connection with huge loans to Hanbo Steel, which was declared insolvent on January 23 after racking up $5.8 billion in loans.
"The prosecution's announcement totally ignored the people's aspiration," Shin said. "We can't help but rely on the people's power to uncover the truth."
She said the National Congress for New Politics would seek a televised hearing during a separate parliamentary probe, for which a special commitee had already been formed in the National Assembly.

Shin did not say if her party sought to begin yet another probe by independent prosecutors but a National Congress official said the party would seek legislation to allow them to restart the prosecution probe.
